correctness.rationale: Derive the exact neighbor-XOR rule and conjugate the two cyclic rows to a 2x2 Jordan block with f=(z^2+z+1)/z. q=z^2+z+1 has roots of order three, giving the iff reversibility threshold. When 3 divides the circumference, CRT isolates a 2t-dimensional q-primary factor per row, J nilpotent of sharp index max(2,t), giving 2^(2n-4t) periodic states and sharp transient bound. For dyadic n, Frobenius powers reduce fixed vectors to shift-invariant rows and F0 to shift-4 invariants; differences of exact fixed counts yield all primitive cycle numbers. Recomputed exact Gaussian ranks for n=3..36 and dyadic n=4..64; exhausted all 256 and 65,536 configurations for n=4,8. Finite tests are supporting evidence only; unrestricted result follows from proof.

originality.rationale: The complete 2023 graph-cellular-automaton work studies conforming/non-conformist rules and random-regular-network behavior, not exact arithmetic orbit counts on cubic prisms. The complete published results for binary parity on Hamming distance-two cubes and complete multipartite networks have incompatible graph hypotheses and uniformly bounded cycle lengths; neither implies the three-divisibility reversibility criterion, the nonreversible periodic-core dimension and transient depth, or the all-state dyadic-prism cycle census. The 2008 graph-CA survey is background. Generic linear finite-dynamical-system theory and Rule-150 techniques are acknowledged and do not, in the inspected materials, state this full two-layer prism classification. Priority remains uncertain against possible earlier equivalent additive-CA/module formulations.
residual_risks: Earlier additive one-dimensional cellular automata or finite-field linear dynamical-system literature may imply the prism formulas under alternate terms; a relevant 2005 general linear finite-systems article was not fully inspected.
Semantic searches and title scans are incomplete; they establish no uniqueness theorem or definitive priority.
The claimed value is the complete natural-graph characterization, not novelty of finite-field linear algebra or the XOR/Rule-150 method.

value.rationale: This is a sharp structural reversibility boundary and a complete, naturally indexed orbit count for a canonical connected cubic network. It explains how strongly structured graphs produce arbitrarily long, recurrent opinion disagreement even when random regular network studies emphasize typical short attractors. The modulo-three singularity, nilpotent entry depth, and all-state dyadic counts give mathematical information not implied by a one-row restricted Rule-150 example. The result does not assert a random-ensemble phase transition or a universal graph theorem.
